topics.title: Whole numbers to 100,000
topics.summary: Place value, reading and comparing large numbers.

steps.text: Base-ten blocks: a flat is 100, a rod is 10, a cube is 1. This shows 243.

Each place is 10 times the place on its right:
ones → tens → hundreds → thousands → ten thousands.
In 47,352 the 4 is in the ten thousands place, so it stands for 40,000. The 7 stands for 7,000.

Line the numbers up by place value:
38,415
38,154
Start from the left. 3 = 3, 8 = 8, then 4 > 1. So 38,415 is greater. The first place that differs decides.
Line up ones under ones, tens under tens. Start from the ones.
4,568 + 2,775: ones 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens 6 + 7 + 1 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Keep going: 7,343.

questions.hint: You need to rename across the zero: 6,302 = 62 hundreds + 10 tens… take it one place at a time.
Think 8,999 + 1. Subtract from 8,999 first, then add 1.

topics.title: Factors and multiples
topics.summary: Find factors and multiples of whole numbers.

steps.text: Arrange 12 counters in equal rows. 3 rows of 4 works, so 3 and 4 are factors of 12.

Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, …
A factor divides exactly. A multiple is in the times table.
7 × 4 means 7 groups of 4, or 4 groups of 7. Both make 28.
Use facts you know: 7 × 8 = 7 × 4 × 2 = 28 × 2 = 56.
Think of 243 × 3 as 3 groups of 243 blocks.
Multiply each place: 3 ones × 3 = 9, 4 tens × 3 = 12 tens (write 2, carry 1 hundred), 2 hundreds × 3 + 1 = 7 hundreds. 243 × 3 = 729.
Split the 2-digit number into tens and ones: 34 × 26 = 34 × 20 + 34 × 6.
Share 84 counters into 4 equal groups. Share the 8 tens first (2 tens each), then the 4 ones (1 each). Each group gets 21.
Divide from the left: 8 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens. 4 ones ÷ 4 = 1. So 84 ÷ 4 = 21.
Share 17 sweets among 5 children. Each gets 3, and 2 are left over.
17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2. Check: 5 × 3 + 2 = 17. The remainder is always smaller than the number you divide by.

topics.title: Fractions
topics.summary: Equivalent fractions, and adding and subtracting fractions.

steps.text: Fold a strip of paper in half and shade one half.
Fold it again. Now 2 of 4 parts are shaded. Same amount, so 1/2 = 2/4.
Multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.
2/8 shaded, then 3/8 more. Count the eighths: 5 of them.
The parts are the same size, so add the tops: 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8. Type the top and bottom numbers in the boxes.

topics.title: Decimals
topics.summary: Tenths, and adding and subtracting decimals.

steps.text: Cut a whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth, 0.1. Three parts are 0.3.
2 and 4 tenths is written 2.4. Line up the decimal points to add: 2.4 + 1.5 = 3.9.

topics.title: Word problems with bar models
topics.summary: Draw a bar model, then solve.

steps.text: Ana has 1,250 stickers. Ben has 860. How many altogether? Draw one bar with two parts.

Whole = part + part: 1,250 + 860 = 2,110.
If the whole is known and a part is missing, subtract.
Raj has 340 cards. Mei has 125 more than Raj. Draw two bars. Mei's bar is Raj's bar plus an extra part.

Mei = 340 + 125 = 465.
The extra part is the difference between the two bars.
Lea has 3 times as many shells as Jun. Jun has 24. Draw 1 unit for Jun and 3 equal units for Lea.
1 unit = 24. Altogether there are 4 units: 4 × 24 = 96. Lea alone has 3 units: 72.
